Rexy 360 is designed for '''Rexy Wheels in joystick mode'''. It also works with gamepads, the keyboard, and a range of '''Alt Inputs'''.

== Rexy Wheels and gamepads ==
# Put Rexy Wheels in '''joystick mode''' and plug them in (or connect a gamepad).
# In '''Head — Pan · Tilt · Roll''', click '''Bind''' on an axis, then move the wheel or stick you want. Zoom is bound in '''Lens'''.
# Choose '''Absolute''' or '''Continuous''' under '''Wheels''' (see [[Rexy 360: The virtual head|The virtual head]]).

On a Mac, allow '''Input Monitoring''' the first time a controller is read, then restart Rexy 360 (see [[Installing Rexy 360#Controllers and Input Monitoring|Installing]]).

== Tuning an axis ==
Each axis has Rexy Bridge's tuning controls:
; S : Sensitivity
; C : Curve
; D : Damping
; F : Filter
'''C''' next to an input opens '''calibration''' and the '''Filter Lab'''.

== Alt Inputs ==
Alt Inputs are listed in this order: '''Mouse devices, OSC, MIDI, FreeD, NODO'''.

=== Mouse devices (Windows) ===
Hand wheels that only send a mouse signal over USB can drive Rexy 360 (since 1.0.2-beta).
* Tick '''listen''' and every mouse shows up by name, with its x, y, wheel and buttons.
* '''Bind''' a control and move the one you want.
* It works like an absolute wheel: '''range''' sets how many counts cover a control, '''Zero''' re-centres.

'''Ctrl+M''' detaches the cursor while the wheels drive: the pointer holds still (clicks and scrolling still work) and the wheels keep moving the head. Press Ctrl+M again — or switch to another app — to get the cursor back. It can also be bound in '''Functions'''.

=== OSC, MIDI and FreeD ===
Rexy 360 accepts OSC, MIDI and FreeD as inputs, bound the same way as other controls.

=== NODO Inertia Wheels ===
NODO wheels are read straight from the '''USB Receiver'''. Support is built from NODO's published data format and tested with simulated wheels — please report how it works with yours to rob@realprogear.com.

== Keyboard ==
The keyboard can drive Rexy 360 too, and functions (such as Ctrl+M) can be bound in '''Functions'''.
